papers.title_in_file: Limitations of Quantum Hardware for Molecular Energy Estimation Using VQE
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, results (2.1 to 2.6), conclusions, methods
papers.what_it_is: A VQE study that runs Qubit-ADAPT energy evaluations for benzene on IBM-Torino and uses noise simulations to estimate the coherence times that would be needed.

assertions.value: The authors report that, given the magnitude of the observed errors in benzene energy evaluations on IBM-Torino, reliable VQE optimization on current quantum hardware is unfeasible, and they attribute the large errors to the large number of measurements needed for the full Hamiltonian.
quotes: given the magnitude of the observed errors in molecular energy evaluations, reliable VQE optimization on current quantum hardware remains unfeasible.
The large errors stem from the extensive number of measurements required to evaluate the full Hamiltonian
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one device and one molecule.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is tied to benzene with a reduced active space and to the 2024 era IBM-Torino device; it does not bound what other hardware or molecules can do.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum computer was used only for single-point energy evaluations of ansatz states built from exact classical calculations, and that the benzene active space gave circuits acting on 8 qubits.
assertions.anchor: Section 2.5, p.14, and Section 4 Methods, p.19
quotes: the quantum machine is used exclusively for single-point energy evaluations
resulting in quantum circuits acting on 8 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section 2.5 and Section 4.
assertions.reader_inference: The hardware never ran a full VQE optimization loop in this study, so the title's limitation applies to energy evaluation of fixed ansatz states.

assertions.value: The authors report that thermal-relaxation noise simulations suggest accurate Qubit-ADAPT energies for ansatzes with up to seven operators would need coherence times approximately two orders of magnitude longer than those currently available.
quotes: would necessitate coherence times approximately two orders of magnitude longer than those currently available
assertions.certainty_reason: An extrapolation from simulations with an assumed noise model, one molecule.

papers.title_in_file: A Survey of Classical And Quantum Sequence Models
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, QRNN and QSANN sections, text and image experiments, results and conclusions
papers.what_it_is: A short survey with re-implementations of quantum recurrent and quantum self-attention networks for text and image classification, plus a positional-encoding enhancement.

assertions.value: The authors report that with positional encoding QSANN reached 100% train and test accuracy on the MC task and 90.32% test accuracy on the RP task.
assertions.anchor: Section V.D, Fig. 10, p.5 to p.6
quotes: QSANN can achieve 100% train and test accuracy for the MC task and 100% ptrain and 90.32% test accuracy for the RP task.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from small text datasets, run in simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The datasets are very small, so the accuracy says little about advantage over classical models.

assertions.value: The authors report that after 200 epochs the original QSANN without positional information reached 73% test accuracy on the MC task and 64.5% on the RP task, and they say the RP task depends on word positions.
quotes: After 200 epochs, QSANN achieves 73% test accuracy on MC task
for the RP task QSANN gets 64.5% accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one small experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because of the limitation of quantum simulators and quantum hardware in the near term, they focus on the self-attention model built from several variational circuits with classical post-processing.
quotes: Here, because of the limitation of quantum simulators and quantum hardware in the near term, we focus on the latter.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Section V.B.

assertions.value: The authors state that the RP task has 74 training samples (containing 91 words) and 31 test samples.
quotes: RP task has 74 training samples (containing 91 words) and 31 test samples.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section V.C.
assertions.reader_inference: With 31 test samples one test sample moves accuracy by about 3 points, so 90.32% is 28 of 31.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Simulation on Noisy Superconducting Quantum Computers
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, Section VII error mitigation (all subsections) and conclusion; Sections II to VI skimmed
papers.what_it_is: An IBM tutorial on simulating a tight-binding chain on a noisy superconducting device, with demonstrated error mitigation and circuit optimization.

assertions.value: The authors report that for a longer circuit such as 10 Trotter steps the estimated circuit fidelity rose from 23.0% to 50.5% after transpilation, with the runtime shortened by half.
assertions.anchor: Section VII.B, Fig. 5, p.8 to p.9
quotes: For a longer circuit such as 10 Trotter steps, however,
from 23.0% to 50.5% after transpilation as well as shortening the runtime by half.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical estimate for one circuit family on one device.
assertions.reader_inference: The fidelity values are estimates, not direct measurements of the output state.

assertions.value: The authors report that measurement error mitigation improved the probability amplitudes of a five-qubit GHZ state by 8.9% and 5.2% respectively.
quotes: This is a notable improvement of 8.9% and 5.2% respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device and one state.

assertions.value: The authors report that the combined optimization on ibm_lagos showed much clearer dynamics and good agreement with the expected dynamics for m = 8 Trotter steps.
quotes: the combined optimization in Fig. 8(c,d) shows much clearer dynamics overall with good agreement to the expected dynamics for m = 8 Trotter steps
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical, qualitative result from one device run.

assertions.value: The authors state that post-selection on particle number is a powerful error mitigation option but comes at the cost of potentially throwing out many measurements.
quotes: but comes at the cost of potentially throwing out many measurements
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of a limit of its own method, Section VII.E.

papers.title_in_file: Lagrangian Duality in Quantum Optimization: Overcoming QUBO Limitations for Constrained Problems
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2310.04542 (v2, April 2024), titled in the file as the Lagrangian Duality paper; the file name carries the earlier v1 title. Same paper.
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, theory section on overlap and epsilon, resource-assumption and results sections, conclusion; appendices not read
papers.what_it_is: A theory and numerical-benchmark paper proposing Lagrangian-dual discretized adiabatic quantum computation as an alternative to QUBO penalty encodings for constrained optimization.

assertions.value: The authors report that a numerical benchmarking study suggests the Lagrangian dual DAQC circuits yield a quadratic improvement over QUBO-based circuits in adiabatic evolution time and circuit depth.
assertions.anchor: Section VII Conclusion, and Section VI.E
quotes: which suggests that the proposed Lagrangian dual DAQC circuits yield a quadratic improvement over QUBO-based circuits in terms of adiabatic evolution time and circuit depth
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from numerical benchmarking on binary knapsack instances.
assertions.reader_inference: The benchmark is a simulation on one problem class under noise-free assumptions, so it is not a hardware result.

assertions.value: The authors state, as assumptions for their runtime estimates, that single-qubit and two-qubit gates take 10 and 20 nanoseconds respectively and that all circuit components are noise-free with no overhead for error correction or fault-tolerant quantum computation.
quotes: performs any single-qubit and two-qubit gate operations in 10 and 20 nanoseconds, respectively
All components of the circuit are noise-free; hence there is no overhead for quantum error correction or fault-tolerant quantum computation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup assumptions, Section VI.D.
assertions.reader_inference: The quadratic advantage is stated for an idealized, fault-tolerant, noise-free circuit model, not for current hardware.

assertions.value: The paper derives that for any ϵ > 0 there exist values for T, r and A which yield a unit overlap between the state prepared by LD-DAQC and the eigenstate corresponding to the primal problem.
quotes: for any ϵ > 0, there exist values for T , r and A which yield a unit overlap between the state prepared by LD-DAQC and the eigenstate corresponding to the primal problem
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived analytically from Eq. (15) and Eq. (16), Section IV; the paper itself says the derivation rests on idealized assumptions.
assertions.reader_inference: Reader flags that the paper calls this a derivation under idealized assumptions, not a formal numbered theorem, so the coordinator should confirm the grade.

assertions.value: The authors state that Eq. (15) and Eq. (16) offer intuitive and theoretical insights but are based on idealized assumptions, and that they are not practical for determining the optimal value of T.
quotes: Although Eq. (15) and Eq. (16) offer intuitive and theoretical insights into the LD-DAQC approach, they are based on idealized assumptions.
these equations are not practical for determining the optimal value of T
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of a limit of its own theory, Section IV.

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking Variational Quantum Eigensolvers for Quantum Chemistry
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, benchmarking results (Section 5), discussion; ansatz descriptions (Section 3) skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A simulator-based benchmark of more than ten VQE ansatzes on small molecules, from the MindSpore Quantum team at Huawei.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that most published ansatzes can reach chemical accuracy at the equilibrium points of the tested molecules, but that all the ansatzes failed to have reliable performance at stretched bond lengths.
quotes: we conclude that most published ansatzes can reach chemical accuracy at the equilibrium points of the tested molecules. However, all the ansatzes failed to have reliable performance at stretched bond lengths.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one benchmarking study on simulators.
assertions.reader_inference: Optimizer trapping in local minima may explain part of the failures; the paper itself raises that for some ansatzes.

assertions.value: The authors report that the ADAPT ansatz performs relatively better in smaller molecular systems (below 14 qubits) and usually needs fewer variational parameters, but that it is not scalable for larger molecules.
quotes: The ADAPT ansatz has relatively better performance in smaller molecular systems (below 14 qubits).
It usually needs fewer variational parameters, but it is not scalable for larger molecules.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one benchmarking study; ADAPT was only run on the three smallest molecules.

assertions.value: The authors state that they benchmarked six molecules (8 qubits H4, 12 qubits LiH, 14 qubits BeH2, 14 qubits H2O, 18 qubits CH4 and 20 qubits N2) with MindQuantum as the quantum simulator.
quotes: six representative molecules, including 8 qubits H4, 12 qubits LiH, 14 qubits BeH2, 14 qubits H2O, 18 qubits CH4, and 20 qubits N2
was used as the quantum simulator.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section 5.
assertions.reader_inference: All results are noise-free simulation, so none bears on hardware noise.

assertions.value: The authors state that, due to the RAM limitation, the QCC ansatz was only benchmarked on H4, qubit-ADAPT only on H4 and LiH, and ADAPT on H4, LiH and BeH2.
quotes: Due to the RAM limitation, QCC ansatz was only benchmarked on H4; qubit-ADAPT ansatz was only benchmarked on H4 and LiH; ADAPT ansatz were benchmarked on H4, LiH and BeH2.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of a limit of its own coverage, Section 5.

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking a boson sampler with Hamming nets
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, results, conclusion, supplementary information
papers.what_it_is: A method that builds Hamming-distance networks from boson sampler outcomes and uses logistic regression to tell indistinguishable from distinguishable photons.

assertions.value: The authors report that the machine learning calculations reveal a high accuracy (> 98%) in classifying distinguishable and indistinguishable photon sources.
quotes: The performed ML calculations reveal a high accuracy (> 98%) in classifying distinguishable and indistinguishable photons sources.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the data are simulated.
assertions.reader_inference: The classifier is classical logistic regression applied to samples of a quantum device, so it is ML for characterizing a quantum device and not a quantum model.

assertions.value: The authors state that they used a Boson-Sampling python package to calculate the probability distributions for a given boson sampler matrix U.
quotes: In this work we used Boson-Sampling python package56 to calculate probability distributions
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Supplementary Information.
assertions.reader_inference: The outcomes are drawn from simulated probability distributions, not from a physical boson sampler.

assertions.value: The authors state that the practical realization of the third complexity measure is related to the quantum state tomography problem, which is characterized by considerable limitations on the number of qubits in the system in question.
assertions.anchor: Section on Shannon and von Neumann entropy, p.8
quotes: the practical realization of the third complexity measure is related to quantum state tomography problem, which is characterized by considerable limitations on the number of qubits in the system in question.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of a limit of its own proposed measure.

papers.title_in_file: Hierarchical Multigrid Ansatz for Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, Laplacian eigensolver, combinatorial optimization, conclusion; appendix skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of a multigrid-style growing ansatz for VQE, compared with the Efficient SU(2) hardware-efficient ansatz on a Laplacian eigenproblem, MaxCut and Max-Ek-Sat.

assertions.value: The authors state that they showed improved average performance by comparison with the Efficient SU(2) VQE for the Laplacian eigenvalue problem, as well as for MaxCut and Max-Ek-Sat.
quotes: we showed improved average performance by comparison with the Efficient SU(2) VQE for the Laplacian eigenvalue problem, as well as for MaxCut and Max-Ek-Sat.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from noise-free simulation on small instances.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison uses more optimizer calls for the multigrid method, so it is not an equal-cost comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that the tests were run with Qiskit's Aer simulator assuming that there is no hardware noise, and that they plan to complement the numerical studies with actual hardware studies in the future.
quotes: we run our tests with Qiskit’s Aer simulator, assuming that there is no hardware noise.
in the future, we plan to complement our numerical studies with actual hardware studies on existing NISQ devices
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Section V.A and Section VI.

assertions.value: The authors state that they seeded the hierarchy with an Efficient SU(2) ansatz as a proof of concept, and that this choice is somewhat arbitrary and does not come with a multigrid-related theoretical justification.
quotes: We seed the Multigrid Hierarchy with an Efficient SU(2) ansatz as a proof of concept.
This choice is somewhat arbitrary and does not come with a multigrid-related theoretical justification.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of a limit of its own method, Section IV.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning using the ZXW-Calculus
papers.partial_detail: abstract, Chapter 1 main contributions, Chapter 4 theorem statements, Chapter 6 discussion; proofs and appendices not read
papers.what_it_is: An Oxford MSc thesis that uses the ZXW-calculus to prove parameter-shift gradient rules, a no-go bound on shift terms, and barren plateau results for some ansatzes.

assertions.value: The thesis proves (Theorem 4.16) that it is not possible to compute the gradient of gates with generator eigenvalues −λ, 0, λ using less than four shifts.
quotes: it is not possible to compute the gradient of gates with generator eigenvalues −λ, 0, λ using less than four shifts.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 4.16, Section 4.2.3.
assertions.reader_inference: The thesis author says the proof is, to the best of his knowledge, the first for a conjecture of Anselmetti et al.

assertions.value: The thesis derives a novel, generalised parameter shift rule with 2n terms that is applicable to gates that can be represented with n parametrised spiders in the ZXW-calculus.
quotes: we derive a novel, generalised parameter shift rule with 2n terms that is applicable to gates that can be represented with n parametrised spiders in the ZXW-calculus.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 4.13, Section 4.2.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The thesis notes a possible link to the Wierichs et al. shift rule, which it leaves open.

assertions.value: The author reports that the numerical tool empirically concluded that, even at a single layer, the studied Sim et al. ansatzes likely all have barren plateaus.
quotes: empirically concluded that even at a single layer they likely all have barren plateaus
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from a variance estimate tool, not a proof.

assertions.value: The author states that the numerical tool cannot formally prove or disprove the existence of barren plateaus but gives a good indication of the behaviour of an ansatz for practically used circuit dimensions.
quotes: While the tool cannot formally prove or disprove the existence of barren plateaus, it gives a good indication of the behaviour of an ansatz for practically used circuit dimensions.
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis's statement of a limit of its own tool, Section 6.2.
